label: second copy step (recall_idx 1, input = first original token)
explanation: Fires essentially only at step L+1, the step right after <DEL>, where the input is the first original token fed back and the model outputs original token 1. 99.9% of activations and ~100% of activation mass fall at this position. It never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step itself, or at later copy steps (59 stray activations at recall_idx 2). But it fires on only ~65% of these steps, so precision is incomplete. The firing rate and magnitude depend on sequence length in a U shape: ~90% for L=3, ~66% for L=4, ~40% for L=5-6, ~58% for L=7, ~85% for L=8, ~98% for L=9. L=9 sequences hold ~41% of the activation mass. Token identity also modulates it weakly: the rate is higher when the input/first token is a, c, k or f and when the output token is r, h, f or s, and lower when the output is a digit. Restricting to L in {3,4,7,8,9} raises precision to 0.77 but lowers recall to 0.80, with no F1 gain.
